sentences.text: Portugalosuchus is an extinct genus of eusuchian crocodyliform, a group of crocodile-like reptiles, classified within the family Gavialidae.
If classified as a basal crocodylian, Portugalosuchus would be the oldest known crocodylian.
The genus Portugalosuchus was described by Mateus and colleagues in 2018.
The only known fossils of Portugalosuchus come from the Tentugal Formation in Portugal.
The type species of the genus is Portugalosuchus azenhae, and a 2021 study placed it within Crocodylia as a member of Gavialidae closely related to thoracosaurs like Thoracosaurus.
Portugalosuchus lived during the Cenomanian stage of the Late Cretaceous, dating from 100.5 to 93.9 million years ago.

Researchers have noted that Portugalosuchus might possibly fall outside of Crocodylia entirely, as a 2022 analysis using morphological and DNA data suggested it is outside Crocodylia as the sister taxon to Allodaposuchidae.
